decisions.reason: The source changes the electrical pin-order policy for the interboard power connector, not its physical orientation, placement, accessibility, or mounting-hole clearance.
Allowing the power connector pins to be reordered does not change the power board's dimensions, installation orientation, USB-C placement, aspect ratio, or mounting constraints.
The local context limits the decision to rotating +5V and 3.3V on the power connector; the separate signal connector carrying D+ and D- remains unchanged.
The source concerns power-connector pin ordering and does not change I2C cable length, bus speed, pull-up resistance, or pull-up location.
The charge-status display method and GPIO assignment are independent of the reordered interboard power-connector pins.
The source does not alter the selected addressable LED family, its data GPIO, or its power and logic behavior.
The battery connector is a separate JST-PH three-pin interface; the source only relaxes the pin order of the interboard power connector.
Reordering the +5V and 3.3V connector positions does not change generation, enable control, default state, or usage of the switchable 5V rail.
The NTC terminal, J_BAT connection, and thermal-protection behavior are unaffected by the interboard power-connector pin-order policy.
The source does not change the battery protection controller or its overcharge and overdischarge cutoff behavior.
